meta.title: France 2027 Election Observatory
meta.editorial_note: Non-partisan research. Separate declared candidacy, campaign activity, sponsorship pledges, validated sponsorships and official ballot qualification. Poll averages are not individual polls. Missing poll candidates are not zero.

candidates.name: Marine Le Pen
candidates.campaign_status: Declared candidate; announced 7 July 2026; participated in the 27 August MEDEF debate.
candidates.ballot_status: Declared; eligibility remains subject to the legal process and final sponsorship validation.
candidates.profile: Marine Le Pen announced her candidacy on 7 July 2026. Her appeal judgment and cassation process remain material to eligibility; do not describe her as ballot-qualified.
candidates.policy_summary: Recurring RN priorities include tighter immigration and border controls, national-preference measures, public order and purchasing power, alongside criticism of aspects of EU integration. These are recurring positions, not a substitute for a complete 2027 manifesto.
candidates.programme_status: No full 2027 programme established in this snapshot. Her 2026 MEDEF pensions proposal was a return to 62, with 60 for qualifying long-career workers and 42 contribution years. Legal eligibility remains a separate issue.

candidates.name: Jean-Luc Mélenchon
candidates.campaign_status: Declared candidate; announced 3 May 2026; participated in the 27 August MEDEF debate; presented LFI programme at Le Bourget on 7 November.
candidates.profile: LFI presented its programme on 7 November 2026. Programme proposals are summarised in the linked Reuters report; distinguish party commitments from independent costing.
candidates.policy_summary: LFI’s 7 November 2026 programme proposes a higher net minimum wage, price controls on essentials, wage indexation, higher taxes on wealthy households, reversing the pension reform and a foreign/energy-policy shift including leaving NATO’s integrated command and replacing nuclear power with renewables.
candidates.programme_status: A written 2027 programme was presented at Le Bourget on 7 November 2026. Figures and policy details should be attributed to the LFI programme and independently assessed for cost and feasibility.

candidates.name: Édouard Philippe
candidates.campaign_status: Declared candidate; announced 3 September 2024; participated in the 27 August MEDEF debate.
candidates.profile: Former prime minister and Horizons leader. Rejects a proposed right-centre primary for now; see Le Monde coverage of 3 November 2026.
candidates.policy_summary: Centre-right, liberal-conservative themes include fiscal discipline, economic competitiveness, public-sector reform and pension-system changes. In September 2026 he argued for moving the legal retirement age to 65 within less than ten years, with a funded pillar.
candidates.programme_status: No complete 2027 programme indexed in the 7 November snapshot. Treat earlier government policy and public statements as distinct from a new campaign platform.

candidates.name: Raphaël Glucksmann
candidates.campaign_status: Declared candidate; won the social-democratic primary in October 2026; participated in the 27 August MEDEF debate.
candidates.profile: Won the social-democratic primary on 11 October with 66% in the first round, according to Le Monde. This does not imply unity across the entire left.
candidates.policy_summary: Pro-European social democracy, European sovereignty and defence, support for Ukraine, social investment, industrial policy and ecological transition. He supports reversing the 2023 pension reform and returning to 62, with detailed contribution rules still unclear.
candidates.programme_status: Won the social-democratic primary in October 2026. No complete 2027 programme indexed in the 7 November snapshot.

candidates.name: Gabriel Attal
candidates.campaign_status: Declared candidate; Renaissance leader; participated in the 27 August MEDEF debate; called for a broad primary of the democrats in late October.
candidates.profile: Former prime minister. Advocates a primary to select a broader centre/right candidate; distinguish this from agreement by other contenders.
candidates.policy_summary: Centrist / liberal-reformist themes include work, education, economic competitiveness, public order and state reform. In September 2026 he argued for a duration-based pension system with points and a funded component, without specifying a new legal retirement age.
candidates.programme_status: No complete 2027 programme indexed in the 7 November snapshot. Distinguish his record as prime minister from campaign commitments.

candidates.name: Bruno Retailleau
candidates.campaign_status: Declared candidate; Les Républicains leader; participated in the 27 August MEDEF debate.
candidates.profile: Conservative right contender. Debate statements on pensions and the economy are recorded separately from a full 2027 programme.
candidates.policy_summary: Conservative-right priorities include immigration control, public order, authority and fiscal restraint. In 2026 he proposed a minimum retirement age of 63, a full-rate age of 65 and a funded component for new entrants.
candidates.programme_status: No complete 2027 programme indexed in the 7 November snapshot. The pension figures are attributed public statements, not a full manifesto.

candidates.name: Marine Tondelier
candidates.campaign_status: Declared candidate; Les Écologistes leader; participated in the 27 August MEDEF debate.
candidates.profile: Green party leader. The 27 August MEDEF debate establishes active campaign participation; the 2027 programme should be sourced separately.
candidates.policy_summary: Green politics centred on climate action, biodiversity, ecological planning, public transport, energy transition, renovation, food systems and social protection. In 2026 she supported reversing the pension reform, initially returning to 62 with an eventual 60 for early starters or arduous work.
candidates.programme_status: No complete 2027 programme indexed in the 7 November snapshot. Financing details on pensions remain incomplete; sponsorship viability and left-wing alliances remain open questions.

candidates.name: David Lisnard
candidates.campaign_status: Declared contender; Nouvelle Énergie leader; campaigning and involved in the centre-right primary debate.
candidates.ballot_status: Declared contender; not yet officially qualified.
candidates.profile: Mayor of Cannes and Nouvelle Énergie leader. Do not infer validated sponsorships from announced pledges.
candidates.policy_summary: Liberal-right themes include lower taxes and spending, economic freedom, local government and public order. His earlier pension positions include keeping the 2023 reform and adding a collective funded pillar.
candidates.programme_status: No complete 2027 programme indexed in the 7 November snapshot. Some policy evidence predates the current campaign; do not treat older positions as newly costed 2027 promises.

candidates.name: Éric Zemmour
candidates.campaign_status: Declared contender; Reconquête! leader; previously ran in 2022.
candidates.ballot_status: Declared contender; not yet officially qualified.
candidates.profile: Political commentator and Reconquête! leader. Current campaign proposals require candidate-specific 2027 sourcing.
candidates.policy_summary: National-conservative / far-right politics focused on sharply restricting immigration, assimilation, national identity and revising France’s relationship with the EU. In September 2026 he discussed raising the legal retirement age to 64 or 65 by 2030.
candidates.programme_status: No detailed 2027 programme established in this snapshot. The 2022 platform is not automatically the 2027 platform.

candidates.name: François Ruffin
candidates.campaign_status: Declared contender; has said he is a candidate for the presidency; released 40 proposals in a book on 6 November, while saying it is not a formal programme.
candidates.ballot_status: Declared contender; not yet officially qualified.
candidates.profile: Debout! deputy. Le Parisien reported on 6 November that he published 40 proposals but described the book as not being a programme; reported readiness to withdraw in the sponsorship context should be tracked separately.
candidates.policy_summary: Left-wing, labour-focused and economically interventionist themes include industrial rebuilding, domestic production, worker protections and climate transition. His November 2026 book set out 40 proposals on industrial, demographic and climate challenges, but he said it was not a formal programme.
candidates.programme_status: The book “Au boulot !” is explicitly not presented by Ruffin as a manifesto. He has said he could withdraw if a viable route to defeating Marine Le Pen emerged, but not in favour of Mélenchon.

candidates.name: Fabien Roussel
candidates.campaign_status: Declared contender; PCF national secretary; announced candidacy in September 2026.
candidates.ballot_status: Declared contender; not yet officially qualified.
candidates.profile: PCF leader. Formal status and any party ratification should be checked against primary party sources.
candidates.policy_summary: Communist / left politics traditionally prioritises wages, purchasing power, industrial sovereignty, public services and workers’ interests. No sufficiently recent quantified 2026 pension position was found in the research workbook.
candidates.programme_status: No complete 2027 programme indexed in the 7 November snapshot. Older positions should not be presented as current without new evidence.

candidates.name: Nicolas Dupont-Aignan
candidates.campaign_status: Declared contender; Debout la France leader.
candidates.ballot_status: Declared contender; not yet officially qualified.
candidates.profile: Former presidential candidate and leader of Debout la France. Current programme needs direct sourcing.
candidates.policy_summary: Sovereigntist right themes include national independence, criticism of EU integration, purchasing power and public services. In October 2026 he proposed maintaining the retirement age at 62 years and nine months and creating a funded account for each newborn.
candidates.programme_status: No complete 2027 programme indexed in the 7 November snapshot. The pension proposal is a specific public statement, not a full programme.

candidates.name: Natacha Polony
candidates.campaign_status: Declared contender; founded Nous sommes la France movement.
candidates.ballot_status: Declared contender; not yet officially qualified.
candidates.profile: Journalist and essayist. Her self-description and external ideological classifications should be kept distinct.
candidates.policy_summary: Sovereigntist and republican themes include national sovereignty, education, industrial policy, secular republicanism and social cohesion. Her self-description as a left sovereigntist should be distinguished from outside ideological classifications.
candidates.programme_status: No complete 2027 programme indexed in the 7 November snapshot. Public interviews and speeches should be attributed individually.

candidates.name: Xavier Bertrand
candidates.campaign_status: Potential contender; not confirmed as a formal candidate in the current baseline.
candidates.profile: Centre-right political figure; keep as potential rather than declared until a clear announcement is sourced.
candidates.policy_summary: Centre-right / social-Gaullist themes include industrial employment, regional development, public services and security.
candidates.programme_status: Potential contender in this research snapshot, not confirmed as a formal candidate. No complete 2027 programme indexed.

candidates.name: Nathalie Arthaud
candidates.campaign_status: Declared contender; Lutte ouvrière spokesperson and repeat presidential candidate.
candidates.ballot_status: Declared contender; not yet officially qualified.
candidates.profile: Lutte ouvrière spokesperson. Confirm 2027 campaign details with party sources.
candidates.policy_summary: Far-left / Trotskyist politics centred on workers’ interests, class struggle, redistribution and opposition to capitalism. Her September 2026 speech criticised Le Pen’s pension proposal but did not set out a quantified alternative retirement age.
candidates.programme_status: No quantified 2027 pension proposal identified in the research workbook. Check Lutte ouvrière’s official campaign material for current programme details.

candidates.name: Bruno Le Maire
candidates.campaign_status: Probable / potential contender; programme material indexed by Observatoire 2027, but formal status requires verification.
candidates.profile: Former finance minister. Observatoire 2027 lists him as probable; do not present him as formally declared without a direct announcement.
candidates.policy_summary: Centre-right economic policy themes include fiscal policy, debt, competitiveness and institutional reform, based on positions indexed by Observatoire 2027.
candidates.programme_status: Listed as probable by Observatoire 2027 in the 7 November snapshot. A formal candidacy and complete 2027 programme have not been verified here.

news.title: French presidential hopeful Mélenchon pledges economic stimulus, renews NATO exit call
news.summary: Reuters reports LFI’s programme launch at Le Bourget, including a higher net minimum wage, price controls, pension changes, tax proposals, NATO policy and an energy transition away from nuclear power.

source.title: French presidential hopeful Mélenchon pledges economic stimulus, renews NATO exit call

news.title: « Ici est la force ! » : depuis Le Bourget, Jean-Luc Mélenchon prêt à décoller pour le second tour
news.summary: Coverage of Mélenchon’s 7 November rally at Le Bourget and the launch of his campaign programme. Attendance figures are claims by organisers unless independently verified.

source.title: « Ici est la force ! » : depuis Le Bourget, Jean-Luc Mélenchon prêt à décoller pour le second tour

news.title: En meeting au Bourget, Mélenchon mobilise sa base tout en cherchant à élargir son électorat
news.summary: Le Monde analyses Mélenchon’s 7 November rally and programme launch, noting both the mobilisation of his core supporters and his effort to broaden his appeal.

source.title: En meeting au Bourget, Mélenchon mobilise sa base tout en cherchant à élargir son électorat

news.title: Présidentielle 2027 : les sondages ont-ils toujours vu juste à six mois des élections ?
news.summary: A look at the limits of interpreting polls months before an election, including the effect of candidate line-ups and campaign developments.

source.title: Présidentielle 2027 : les sondages ont-ils toujours vu juste à six mois des élections ?

news.title: Présidentielle 2027 : l’hypothèse d’une candidature de Christine Lagarde questionne à droite et au sein du bloc central
news.summary: Le Monde examines speculation about Christine Lagarde after her announced early departure from the ECB. The article notes there is no clear evidence of an organised campaign.

source.title: Présidentielle 2027 : l’hypothèse d’une candidature de Christine Lagarde questionne à droite et au sein du bloc central

news.title: « Au boulot ! » : François Ruffin dévoile 40 propositions dans un livre, qui n’est « pas un programme »
news.summary: Ruffin presented 40 proposals in a book while explicitly distinguishing it from a formal campaign programme. He also left open the possibility of withdrawing if a viable alternative to Marine Le Pen emerged, while ruling out Mélenchon as that solution.

source.title: « Au boulot ! » : François Ruffin dévoile 40 propositions dans un livre, qui n’est « pas un programme »

news.title: Meeting de Mélenchon : une création artistique collective illustrera le programme présidentiel de LFI
news.summary: Preview of the artistic presentation planned for LFI’s programme launch at Le Bourget.

source.title: Meeting de Mélenchon : une création artistique collective illustrera le programme présidentiel de LFI

news.title: Présidentielle 2027 : la primaire de la droite et du centre a du plomb dans l’aile avant même d’avoir décollé
news.summary: The proposed centre-right primary faces disagreement over who should participate. Gabriel Attal supports a broad selection process while Édouard Philippe resists it; other parties disagree on the perimeter.

source.title: Présidentielle 2027 : la primaire de la droite et du centre a du plomb dans l’aile avant même d’avoir décollé

news.title: Gérald Darmanin rejette la primaire voulue par Gabriel Attal et appelle à se rassembler derrière Edouard Philippe
news.summary: Justice minister Gérald Darmanin rejected Attal’s proposed primary and called for support to rally behind Édouard Philippe. This is a political endorsement, not evidence that a primary has formally been cancelled.

source.title: Gérald Darmanin rejette la primaire voulue par Gabriel Attal et appelle à se rassembler derrière Edouard Philippe

news.title: Présidentielle 2027 : qui sont les principaux candidats déclarés ou probables ?
